title: Inequality Measurement, Decomposition, and Poverty Analysis
text: release responds feedback Frank Cowell Emmanuel Flachaire v0.1.0 release. Bootstrap CIs every measure. iq_theil, iq_atkinson, iq_sgini, iq_palma, iq_hoover, iq_kolm, iq_percentile_ratio, iq_polarisation, iq_shares, iq_concentration, iq_kakwani, iq_poverty gain ci, R, level arguments. iq_compare() runs single bootstrap loop propagates CIs every row. Negative values supported. Gini, S-Gini, top shares, Palma, Hoover, Wolfson, Kakwani, iq_compare() accept negatives = "keep" distributions containing negatives (wealth, post-tax income). Raffinetti et al. (2017) normalised Gini. iq_gini(x, negatives = "keep", normalised = TRUE) rescales index back [0, 1] negatives present. Wagstaff correction added iq_concentration alongside existing Erreygers correction. iq_kakwani bug fix. post-tax Gini longer takes absolute value negative net incomes, Reynolds-Smolensky index honest high tax burdens.

what: inequality: Inequality Measurement, Decomposition, and Poverty Analysis — inequality-package
title: inequality: Inequality Measurement, Decomposition, and Poverty Analysis — inequality-package
text: Tools measuring income wealth inequality. Computes Gini coefficient bootstrap asymptotic confidence intervals following Davidson (2009) doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2008.11.004 , extended S-Gini family, Theil T L indices (generalised entropy family), Atkinson index, Kolm absolute inequality index, Palma ratio, Hoover index, percentile ratios, Lorenz curves. Supports -within group decomposition following Bourguignon (1979) doi:10.2307/1914138 , income share tabulation, concentration indices health inequality Erreygers (2009) correction, Kakwani tax progressivity Reynolds-Smolensky redistribution indices, Foster-Greer-Thorbecke poverty measures including Sen index, growth incidence curves following Ravallion Chen (2003) doi:10.1016/S0165-1765(02)00205-7 , Wolfson polarisation. functions accept optional survey weights work data source.

title: Atkinson index — iq_atkinson
text: Computes Atkinson inequality index, incorporates explicit normative judgement inequality aversion parameter epsilon. Higher epsilon gives weight transfers bottom distribution.

title: Atkinson index — iq_atkinson
code: iq_atkinson(   x,   weights = NULL,   epsilon = 0.5,   na.rm = FALSE,   ci = FALSE,   R = 1000L,   level = 0.95 )

title: Atkinson index — iq_atkinson
text: x Numeric vector incomes (strictly positive). weights Optional numeric vector survey weights. epsilon Numeric. Inequality aversion parameter (> 0). Default 0.5. Common values: 0.5 (moderate), 1.0 (high), 2.0 (high aversion). na.rm Logical. Remove NA values? Default FALSE. ci Logical. Compute bootstrap confidence intervals? Default FALSE. R Integer. Number bootstrap replicates. Default 1000. level Numeric. Confidence level. Default 0.95.

title: Atkinson index — iq_atkinson
text: S3 object class "iq_atkinson" elements: value Numeric. Atkinson index (0 1). epsilon Numeric. inequality aversion parameter used. ede Numeric. equally distributed equivalent income. mean_income Numeric. mean income. n Integer. Number observations. se, ci_lower, ci_upper, level Bootstrap CI fields, NULL unless ci = TRUE.

title: Atkinson index — iq_atkinson
text: Atkinson index involves either power transformation x^(1 - epsilon) log(x) (epsilon = 1) requires strictly positive values. Use Gini, S-Gini, Kolm index distributions include zeros negatives.

title: Atkinson index — iq_atkinson
text: Atkinson, . B. (1970). "Measurement Inequality." Journal Economic Theory, 2(3), 244–263. Biewen, M. Jenkins, S. P. (2006). "Variance Estimation Generalized Entropy Atkinson Inequality Indices: Complex Survey Data Case." Oxford Bulletin Economics Statistics, 68(3), 371–383.

title: Compare inequality measures — iq_compare
text: x Numeric vector incomes (strictly positive default; see negatives). weights Optional numeric vector survey weights. na.rm Logical. Remove NA values? Default FALSE. ci Logical. Compute bootstrap CIs every measure table? Default FALSE. R Integer. Number bootstrap replicates. Default 1000. level Numeric. Confidence level. Default 0.95. negatives Character. "error" (default) requires strictly positive x; "keep" permits zero negative values, NA returned measures undefined values.

title: Compare inequality measures — iq_compare
text: S3 object class "iq_comparison" elements: table data.frame columns measure, value, (ci = TRUE) ci_lower ci_upper. n Integer. Number observations. level Numeric NULL. Confidence level.

title: Compare inequality measures — iq_compare
text: ci = TRUE function runs single bootstrap loop, recomputing every measure resample. far cheaper calling measure ci = TRUE produces CI every row table. default iq_compare() requires strictly positive values Theil Atkinson rows mathematically undefined zero . Pass negatives = "keep" permit zero negative values: Theil Atkinson rows returned NA case, Gini, S-Gini, Kolm, Wolfson, Palma, Hoover percentile-ratio rows computed using formulas appropriate input.

title: Concentration index — iq_concentration
text: Computes concentration index, measures inequality health () variable across income distribution. Unlike Gini coefficient, ranking variable outcome variable different.

title: Concentration index — iq_concentration
code: iq_concentration(   x,   rank,   weights = NULL,   correction = c("none", "erreygers", "wagstaff"),   bounds = c(0, 1),   na.rm = FALSE,   ci = FALSE,   R = 1000L,   level = 0.95 )

title: Concentration index — iq_concentration
text: x Numeric vector outcome values (e.g. health expenditure). rank Numeric vector ranking values (e.g. income). Must length x. weights Optional numeric vector survey weights. correction Character. "none" (default) standard index; "erreygers" Erreygers (2009) bounded-variable correction; "wagstaff" Wagstaff (2005) normalised index. bounds Numeric vector length 2 giving lower upper bounds x. Required correction = "erreygers". Default c(0, 1) (suitable binary proportion variables). na.rm Logical. Remove NA values? Default FALSE. ci Logical. Compute bootstrap confidence intervals? Default FALSE. R Integer. Number bootstrap replicates. Default 1000. level Numeric. Confidence level. Default 0.95.

title: Concentration index — iq_concentration
text: S3 object class "iq_concentration" elements: value Numeric. concentration index. correction Character. correction applied. n Integer. Number observations. se, ci_lower, ci_upper, level Bootstrap CI fields, NULL unless ci = TRUE.

title: Concentration index — iq_concentration
text: positive value indicates outcome concentrated among better-; negative value indicates concentration among worse-. bounded variables (e.g. binary health indicators), standard concentration index bounds depend mean. Two corrections available: correction = "erreygers": Erreygers (2009) corrected index, E = 4 * mu / (b - ) * C, fixed bounds -1 1. correction = "wagstaff": Wagstaff (2005) normalised index, W = C / (1 - mu / b) variables bounded b, standard normalisation much health-economics literature.

title: Concentration index — iq_concentration
text: Wagstaff, ., Paci, P. van Doorslaer, E. (1991). "Measurement Inequalities Health." Social Science Medicine, 33(5), 545–557. Erreygers, G. (2009). "Correcting Concentration Index." Journal Health Economics, 28(2), 504–515. Wagstaff, . (2005). "Bounds Concentration Index Variable Interest Binary, Application Immunization Inequality." Health Economics, 14(4), 429–432.

title: Concentration index — iq_concentration
code: set.seed(1) income <- rlnorm(200, 10, 0.8) health_exp <- income * 0.05 + rnorm(200, 500, 100) iq_concentration(health_exp, rank = income) #>  #> ── Concentration Index ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Value: 0.3065 #> • Observations: 200  # With bootstrap CIs iq_concentration(health_exp, rank = income, ci = TRUE, R = 200) #>  #> ── Concentration Index ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Value: 0.3065 #> • Observations: 200 #> • Bootstrap 95% CI: [0.2691, 0.3359]  # Binary outcome with Erreygers correction sick <- as.numeric(income < median(income)) + rbinom(200, 1, 0.1) sick <- pmin(sick, 1) iq_concentration(sick, rank = income, correction = "erreygers") #>  #> ── Concentration Index (Erreygers) ───────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Value: -0.9241 #> • Observations: 200

title: Between-within group decomposition — iq_decompose
text: Decomposes generalised entropy index -group component (inequality due differences group means) within-group component (inequality within group). decomposition exact: + within = total.

title: Between-within group decomposition — iq_decompose
code: iq_decompose(x, group, weights = NULL, index = "T", na.rm = FALSE)

title: Between-within group decomposition — iq_decompose
text: x Numeric vector incomes (strictly positive). group Factor character vector identifying group membership. weights Optional numeric vector survey weights. index Character numeric. "T" Theil T (GE(1)), "L" mean log deviation (GE(0)), numeric alpha. Default "T". na.rm Logical. Remove NA values? Default FALSE.

title: Between-within group decomposition — iq_decompose
text: S3 object class "iq_decomposition" elements: total Numeric. total GE index. Numeric. -group component. within Numeric. within-group component. groups data.frame columns group, n, mean_income, pop_share, income_share, within_ge. index_name Character. Name index used.

title: Between-within group decomposition — iq_decompose

title: Gini coefficient — iq_gini
text: Computes Gini coefficient distribution, optional survey weights confidence intervals (bootstrap asymptotic).

title: Gini coefficient — iq_gini
code: iq_gini(   x,   weights = NULL,   na.rm = FALSE,   ci = FALSE,   method = c("bootstrap", "asymptotic"),   R = 1000L,   level = 0.95,   negatives = c("error", "keep"),   normalised = FALSE )

title: Gini coefficient — iq_gini
text: x Numeric vector incomes values. weights Optional numeric vector survey weights. na.rm Logical. Remove NA values? Default FALSE. ci Logical. Compute confidence intervals? Default FALSE. method Character. CI method: "bootstrap" (default) "asymptotic" (jackknife-based, faster large samples). R Integer. Number bootstrap replicates (ignored asymptotic). Default 1000. level Numeric. Confidence level. Default 0.95. negatives Character. "error" (default) aborts x contains negative values; "keep" permits negatives. normalised Logical. Use Raffinetti, Siletti Vernizzi (2017) normalised Gini? Default FALSE. meaningful negatives = "keep".

title: Gini coefficient — iq_gini
text: S3 object class "iq_gini" elements: gini Numeric. Gini coefficient (NA undefined). n Integer. Number observations. se Numeric NULL. Standard error. ci_lower Numeric NULL. Lower bound CI. ci_upper Numeric NULL. Upper bound CI. level Numeric NULL. Confidence level. method Character NULL. CI method used. has_negatives Logical. Whether input contained negatives. normalised Logical. Whether Raffinetti et al. normalisation applied.

title: Gini coefficient — iq_gini
text: strictly non-negative distribution Gini ranges 0 (perfect equality) 1 (perfect inequality) equals twice area Lorenz curve 45-degree line. Following feedback Cowell Flachaire (personal communication, 2026) package permits negative values via negatives = "keep". Two policies available: normalised = FALSE (default): standard formula applied. negatives present index longer bounded unit interval. population mean non-positive Gini inequality interpretation function returns NA warning. normalised = TRUE: Raffinetti, Siletti Vernizzi (2017) normalised Gini, rescales index back unit interval distributions containing negatives. denominator replaced mean(|x|) index well-defined whenever observation non-zero.

title: Gini coefficient — iq_gini
text: Gini, C. (1912). "Variabilita e mutabilita." Reprinted Memorie di metodologica statistica (Ed. Pizetti E, Salvemini, T). Rome: Libreria Eredi Virgilio Veschi. Davidson, R. (2009). "Reliable Inference Gini Index." Journal Econometrics, 150(1), 30–40. Raffinetti, E., Siletti, E. Vernizzi, . (2017). "Analyzing Effects Negative Non-negative Values Income Inequality: Evidence Survey Household Income Wealth Bank Italy (2012)." Social Indicators Research, 133(1), 185–207.

title: Gini coefficient — iq_gini
code: d <- iq_sample_data("income") iq_gini(d$income) #>  #> ── Gini Coefficient ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Gini: 0.43 #> • Observations: 1000  # Bootstrap CIs iq_gini(d$income, ci = TRUE, R = 500) #>  #> ── Gini Coefficient ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Gini: 0.43 #> • Observations: 1000 #> • Bootstrap 95% CI: [0.4059, 0.4557]  # Asymptotic CIs (faster for large samples) iq_gini(d$income, ci = TRUE, method = "asymptotic") #>  #> ── Gini Coefficient ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Gini: 0.43 #> • Observations: 1000 #> • Asymptotic 95% CI: [0.4065, 0.4534]  # Wealth distributions can include negative net worth wealth <- c(-5000, -1000, 0, 5000, 20000, 80000, 250000) iq_gini(wealth, negatives = "keep") #>  #> ── Gini Coefficient ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Gini: 0.7753 #> • Observations: 7 #> ! Input contains negative values; the standard Gini is not bounded in the unit #>   interval.  # Same data with the Raffinetti et al. (2017) normalisation iq_gini(wealth, negatives = "keep", normalised = TRUE) #>  #> ── Gini Coefficient (Raffinetti et al. normalised) ───────────────────────────── #> • Gini: 0.7495 #> • Observations: 7  # Perfect equality iq_gini(rep(100, 50)) #>  #> ── Gini Coefficient ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> • Gini: 0 #> • Observations: 50

title: Kakwani progressivity index — iq_kakwani

title: Theil index and generalised entropy measures — iq_theil
text: Generalised entropy indices class inequality measures decomposable population subgroups satisfy transfer principle. Higher values indicate inequality. Theil T (GE(1)) Theil L (GE(0)) involve log(x) require strictly positive values. GE(alpha) alpha > 1 well-defined non-negative x highly sensitive small zero values. wealth income net taxes/transfers (can zero negative) use Gini, S-Gini, Kolm index instead. Note cross-validation ineq: package uses textbook GE(alpha) convention, index = "T" GE(1) (Theil T) index = "L" GE(0) (mean log deviation). legacy ineq package uses opposite indexing, ineq::Theil(x, parameter = 0) matches iq_theil(x, "T") ineq::Theil(x, parameter = 1) matches iq_theil(x, "L").

title: inequality 0.2.0
text: release responds feedback Frank Cowell Emmanuel Flachaire (personal communication, 1 May 2026) v0.1.0 release. Two gaps flagged: confidence intervals available Gini, package rejected non-positive values Gini top shares. follow-internal audit produced several smaller fixes ship together.

what: Confidence intervals on every inequality measure
title: inequality 0.2.0
text: Bootstrap confidence intervals now available every inequality function via ci = TRUE. function gains ci, R, level arguments matching existing Gini API. Results returned ci_lower, ci_upper, se fields output object shown print method. Functions extended: iq_theil(), iq_atkinson(), iq_sgini(), iq_palma(), iq_hoover(), iq_kolm(), iq_percentile_ratio(), iq_polarisation(), iq_shares(), iq_concentration(), iq_kakwani(), iq_poverty(). bootstrap uses probability-proportional resampling, survey weights flow variance, just point estimate.

what: iq_compare() runs one bootstrap loop, propagates CIs to every row
title: inequality 0.2.0
text: ci = TRUE, iq_compare() now runs single resample loop attaches ci_lower ci_upper columns every row table. old gini_ci field removed. table now also covers S-Gini, Kolm, Wolfson (12 measures, 9).

what: Negative values are now supported via negatives = "keep"
title: inequality 0.2.0
text: Functions mathematically defined distributions containing negative values now accept negatives = c("error", "keep"), "error" default back-compatibility. negatives = "keep": iq_gini() iq_sgini() permit negatives; index still computed standard formula longer bounded [0, 1]. print method emits note input contains negatives. iq_shares() permits negatives; segment shares may fall outside [0, 1] warning issued. total income non-positive, function returns NA shares warning. iq_palma(), iq_hoover(), iq_polarisation() similarly accept negatives. iq_kolm() already worked negative values unchanged. iq_atkinson() iq_theil() continue require strictly positive values: involve log(x) x^(1 - epsilon) formula mathematically undefined zero . error message now documents explicitly.

title: inequality 0.2.0
text: iq_kakwani() longer takes absolute value post-tax income computing post-tax Gini. Households whose post-tax income negative now reflected honestly Reynolds-Smolensky index. iq_palma() iq_polarisation() now warn rather abort relevant denominator non-positive (returning NA). standard Gini now returns NA (warning) population mean non-positive. Previously function returned 0 mu == 0, conflated “perfect equality” “undefined”. negatives = "keep" set, user pointed normalised = TRUE Raffinetti et al. (2017) bounded variant. Watts poverty index drops observations x = 0 Watts sum (since log(line / 0) diverges) emits one-time warning. FGT measures Sen index continue include poor observations. iq_percentile_ratio() now warns lower percentile negative, since resulting ratio sign-flips inequality interpretation. error message measures require strictly positive input (Theil, Atkinson, decompose, growth_incidence) longer suggests setting negatives = "keep", wrappers expose. Instead message points user measures admit zero negative support.
